title: Directions (Q61-63): Read the passage and answer the questions
passage: During the onset of an El Niño, a burst of westerly winds often occurs over the western equatorial Pacific and the easterly trade winds weaken. The disturbance generates downwelling equatorial Kelvin waves that travel eastward along the thermocline, deepening it in the east. Sea surface temperature rises in the central and eastern Pacific, the edge of the warm pool and the region of deep convection shift eastward, and the zonal atmospheric overturning weakens. Along the coast of Peru, the supply of nutrients to the surface layer drops.

title: Directions (Q98-100): Read the passage and answer the questions
passage: The Interdecadal Pacific Oscillation (IPO) was predominantly in its positive phase from about 1976 to 1998, a period of rapid rise in global mean surface temperature. After the shift to the negative phase around 1998–99, the equatorial trade winds strengthened, the eastern tropical Pacific cooled relative to the long-term trend, and the rise in global surface temperature slowed until about 2013. During this period, sea level in the western tropical Pacific rose much faster than the global mean.
